I am 65 years old. I have farmed for 50 years, since I was 15. My father taught me, and after he passed I learned by watching my neighbors and doing it myself. I finished middle school, so I can read the seed bags and talk to the input dealer, but what I trust is my own two hands and what I see in Lao Wang's field next door.

My farm is only 1.7 mu. It is small, but it is my land. My son works in the county town, so it is mostly me and my wife doing the labor. With 1.7 mu, every yuan matters. I cannot afford a bad year. Last year I planted spring maize, and this year I will do exactly the same — on a plot this small, change is dangerous.

Last year I bought two and a half packages of hybrid seed, about one package per mu. The dealer says these hybrids yield more, and I saw it work on Lao Zhang's plot, so I pay the extra money. I rotary tilled the field in late April before planting. I do not plow deep — the rotary tiller is enough and saves diesel.

For fertilizer, I bought three bags of compound fertilizer from the dealer. Each bag is 100 jin. That is about 80 jin per mu for my 1.7 mu. I spread it all as base fertilizer before planting. I thought about buying urea for topdressing at jointing, but the compound already cost me over 300 yuan, and Lao Wang said his maize did fine with just the compound. I would rather put a little extra base fertilizer than risk the plants going hungry. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing half my yield is a disaster.

I irrigated twice last year — once right after planting because the soil was dry, and once when the plants were knee-high in June. My well is good, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not water for no reason. Two times was enough.

For pests, I sprayed herbicide once after the seedlings came up, and insecticide twice — once when the leaves started showing holes, and once when the cobs were forming. Armyworms and corn borers always come around here, so I do not wait. That is three sprays total.

I got about 1000 jin per mu last year. The dealer price was around 1.6 yuan per jin. If the weather is normal this year, I expect the same — 1000 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if the rains come at the right time. I am sticking with what worked.
